components.css: .ds-nav{display:grid;gap:2px;width:240px;background:var(--sidebar);padding:8px;font:400 14px/20px 'Geist Variable',sans-serif}.ds-nav a{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:center;height:36px;padding:0 28px 0 8px;border-radius:4px;color:color-mix(in oklab,var(--foreground) 72%,transparent);text-decoration:none;transition:background-color 150ms,color 150ms}.ds-nav a:hover{background:var(--sidebar-accent);color:var(--foreground)}.ds-nav a:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ring);outline-offset:-2px}.ds-nav a[aria-current=page]{background:var(--sidebar-accent);color:var(--foreground);font-weight:500}.ds-nav a[aria-current=page]::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset-inline-end:12px;top:50%;margin-top:-3.5px;width:7px;height:7px;border-radius:1.5px;background:var(--seal);animation:ds-stamp 220ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1) both}@keyframes ds-stamp{from{opacity:0;transform:scale(1.9) rotate(-14deg)}to{opacity:1;transform:scale(1) rotate(-6deg)}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-nav a[aria-current=page]::after{animation:none;transform:rotate(-6deg)}}

narrative.overview:
Sekisho is the checkpoint that inspects every pass. The interface is a sumi-ink ledger: warm charcoal grounds (or washi paper in the light theme), kinari off-white ink, ruled with 1px hairlines. One shu-vermilion seal ink marks approval acts and nothing else. The operator should always be able to see where they are, what passed and what was stopped; approving something feels like stamping a pass.

It is an operational interface first: dense, legible, built from adapted Shadcn Admin primitives for long sessions in dim rooms beside terminals and editors. The world is carried by material (ink, paper, hairline, seal) rather than decoration. The dark theme is the default (`defaultTheme="dark"`); the light theme is a full washi-paper variant with its own tuned values, not an inversion. The implementation lives in `web/src/styles.css` and `web/src/components/`; update the tokens and this document together when an intentional design change is made. There are no marketing illustrations or decorative charts.
keyCharacteristics: Warm sumi charcoal grounds in three steps: darkest sidebar, canvas, raised paper-dark panels.
One vermilion seal ink reserved for approval acts; everything else is ink and paper.
Three hairline values (border, hairline, input) instead of shadows to structure surfaces.
Crisp small corners: 6px panels, 4px controls, 2px chips and seal marks.
Geist for the interface, Geist Mono only for numbers, IDs and keys; both self-hosted.
One authored motion, the hanko stamp; everything else is short state feedback.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion is the ink of approval: primary actions, the active route, focus, the brand seal, chart ink and activity density. It never decorates, never fills a panel, and never stands in for a status colour.

rules.name: The Withheld Seal Rule
rules.body: A disabled primary action loses its seal: it drops to the neutral muted ground with muted text and no shadow, rather than fading the vermilion.

rules.name: The Icon And Word Rule
rules.body: Status colour never travels alone. Every status chip pairs an icon with text; every warning or error paragraph (`p.text-warning`, `p.text-error`) hangs a 16px triangle or circle icon in its inline-start margin through CSS, so wrapped lines keep one clean edge.

rules.name: The Counted Characters Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is for strings a person copies or compares character by character (keys, IDs, codes, patterns). Ordinary numbers stay in Geist with tabular figures; tables, `time`, `output`, `kbd` and `code` set `tabular-nums` globally.

rules.name: The Ruled Page Rule
rules.body: Separate content with a 1px hairline before reaching for a shadow or a nested card. Cards that sit in the page flow carry a border, not a shadow.

dos: Do reuse the semantic tokens and adapted Shadcn Admin primitives; change `styles.css` and this file together.
Do reserve vermilion for approval acts: primary actions, the active-route seal, focus, the brand seal, chart ink and activity density.
Do drop disabled primaries to the neutral muted ground instead of a faded vermilion.
Do pair every status colour with an icon and text; a success state is stamped with the seal.

Do verify the dark default and the light variant, keyboard navigation, narrow layouts, right-to-left Arabic, and the supported languages (English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic).
Do keep the hanko stamp as the one authored motion and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do distinguish a planned capability from a working action.
donts: Don't use vermilion as a decorative fill, a panel background, or a substitute for a status colour.
Don't add decorative colour gradients, glows, vivid dashboard fills, or arbitrary accent colours; the only patterned ground is the faint ledger ruling behind the tegata pass.
Don't load fonts from an external service; Geist and Geist Mono ship with the app.
Don't alter the seal geometry, recolour it outside the vermilion pair, or use the framed seal below 24px.
Don't display fake business records or performance claims.
Don't rely on color, hover, or icons alone for essential information.
Don't expose SDK configuration details in routine team workflows unless users need them to make a decision.
